items.headline: Penix is back — Falcons roll the Packers 35-14 at Lambeau
items.body: Michael Penix Jr. returned from injury and lit a fire under Atlanta's offense, which had sputtered with backups the first two weeks. The Falcons rattled off 27 straight points to bury Green Bay 35-14 on Thursday night — snapping the Packers' long home-opener win streak and grabbing Atlanta's first W of the season on the road.
items.say: You catch Thursday night? The Falcons went into Lambeau and smoked the Packers 35-14 — their quarterback Penix came back from injury and they scored 27 in a row. You riding with anybody this NFL season?

items.headline: USA edges ahead at Medinah — and Sungjae Im gets a wild break
items.body: The Presidents Cup is live just outside Chicago, and Team USA grabbed a slim 3-2 lead after Thursday's four-ball session — Scottie Scheffler, Justin Thomas and rookie Jackson Koivun all delivering points. The must-see moment: International star Sungjae Im's tee shot ricocheted off a fence post and somehow stayed in play. Friday's foursomes are underway now.
items.say: That big USA-vs-the-world team golf event is going on right outside Chicago — the Americans grabbed an early lead and there was a shot that bounced off a fence post and stayed alive. You play at all, or just watch the majors?

items.headline: Ticket-punch Thursday — Padres, Cubs, White Sox and Guardians all clinch
items.body: Baseball's final week is doing its thing: four teams booked playoff spots on Thursday. The Padres beat the Dodgers 4-2 for a franchise-record third straight postseason trip — Fernando Tatis Jr. and rookie Ethan Salas broke up a no-hit bid in the seventh — while the Cubs, White Sox and Guardians all clinched too. The Dodgers still locked up a first-round bye.
items.say: Four different teams clinched playoff spots on Thursday — the Padres even did it by beating the Dodgers. Baseball's last week is always chaos like this. You got a team still in the hunt?

items.headline: Bracket's set — record-breaking Lynx open vs. the Liberty
items.body: The WNBA playoffs tip Sunday, and the bracket is locked. Top-seeded Minnesota — a 30-plus-win juggernaut and the runaway title favorite — opens against the No. 8 New York Liberty in a rematch of the 2024 Finals. The other first-round series: Golden State's expansion darlings vs. Dallas, Vegas vs. Indiana, and Atlanta vs. Washington. Best-of-three, higher seeds at home.
items.say: The WNBA playoffs start Sunday, and the Minnesota Lynx have been ridiculous all year — they open against New York in a Finals rematch. That new Golden State expansion team even made it. You keep up with the W at all?

items.headline: Taylor Swift drops 'The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore' — with 4 new songs
items.body: Almost a year after the original, Taylor Swift released a deluxe 'Encore' edition of 'The Life of a Showgirl' today with four brand-new tracks: the teased 'Patient Zero,' plus 'Cleveland!,' 'Pink Clouding' and 'Babylon.' She says they came together on a celebratory trip to Sweden with longtime collaborators Max Martin and Shellback, not from the original sessions.
items.say: Taylor Swift just put out a deluxe version of her last album with four new songs on it — wrote them on a trip to Sweden, apparently. The internet's been in full detective mode. You a Swiftie, or Swift-adjacent?

items.headline: Madonna and Charli xcx team up on 'Danceteria Afterhours'
items.body: Two pop generations on one track: Madonna reworked her 'Confessions II' cut 'Danceteria' into 'Danceteria Afterhours' with Charli xcx, out this week. It's a glittery ode to New York club nights — Madonna's verses about the legendary Danceteria club, Charli trading in her own club-kid origin story. Perfectly timed for a big VMAs weekend.
items.say: Madonna and Charli xcx just dropped a song together — a shiny dance track about old New York club nights. Two totally different eras of pop on one song is kind of a fun combo. What's been on your rotation lately?

items.headline: M83 returns to bedroom-synth roots on 'I Wrote You a Letter'
items.body: The 'Midnight City' crew is back: Anthony Gonzalez released M83's 10th album 'I Wrote You a Letter' today on his own label. He set out to recapture the immediacy of his earliest bedroom recordings — imperfect, dreamy, cinematic — and lead single 'Blister Sunrise' opens with a wall of crashing synths before melting into raw piano. Great windows-down driving music.
items.say: New M83 album out today — they're the 'Midnight City' band with the huge, dreamy synth sound. This one's supposed to be more raw and homemade. Perfect for a long drive. You have a genre you always come back to?

items.headline: 'Charlie Harper' opens — a very grown-up love story
items.body: For the date-night crowd: 'Charlie Harper' hits theaters nationwide today, an emotional modern romance with Emilia Jones ('CODA') and Nick Robinson as two twentysomethings who fall for each other while figuring out who they're becoming — she's chasing a chef's career, he's trying to find his footing. It's been building buzz since its festival premiere.
items.say: There's a new romance movie out this weekend — 'Charlie Harper,' with the girl from CODA. Looks like a proper grown-up love story, the messy figuring-it-out kind. You into that, or more of a popcorn-blockbuster person?

items.headline: 'JoJo Fridays' are back — Steel Ball Run resumes on Netflix
items.body: One for the anime crowd: 'Steel Ball Run,' the wildly popular JoJo's Bizarre Adventure saga, resumes on Netflix today with its 2nd Stage, then rolls out a new episode every Friday. It's a bonkers cross-country horse race across 1890s America — one legless ex-jockey, one mysterious outlaw, a $50 million prize — with a slick new opening theme, 'Spin,' by Japanese band Kroi.
items.say: The JoJo's Bizarre Adventure show is back on Netflix today — this arc is a crazy horse race across the old West with these over-the-top powers. New episodes every Friday now. You watch any anime, or is it a total mystery to you?
